title: Statistical modelling of combined sewer overflow: from rain characteristics to overflow rate
affiliations: Institut Polytechnique de Paris, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Statistical modelling of combined sewer overflow: from rain characteristics to overflow rate
detail.abstract: Combined sewer systems are spread across Europe, North America and beyond. However during heavy rainfall, they become saturated and discharge untreated wastewater into waterbodies through combined sewer overflows (CSOs). The relationship between rainfall and CSO discharge is complex and poorly understood because of underlying dynamics of the sewer system and a lack of high-frequency CSO measurements. We present a methodology to model CSO discharge from rainfall characteristics. It is tested on 22 CSOs outputs in the Seine River in Paris monitored over four summer seasons (June–September) from 2020 to 2023 using the data of 5 rain gauges. Beyond good predictive performance of the model, results show that (i) overflow peaks are well represented by a triangular hydrograph, (ii) a ramp function can predict peak size (total volume and maximum overflow) from rainfall characteristics and (iii) better prediction performances is achieved using multiple rain gauges instead of nearest gauge only. Further results show a map of CSOs response to the spatial distribution of rain, providing hints about functioning of the sewer system. This first end-to-end model can be readily applied to any sewer networks as it is lightweight and easy to train. It can support CSO discharge operational forecasting and the development of data-driven models by guiding their architecture design.

title: Strategy as Practice: Thirty Years Young
affiliations: University of Oxford - Said Business School

detail.title: Strategy as Practice: Thirty Years Young
detail.abstract: Thirty years after Long Range Planning published the first article in the field, this Perspective reviews the promise, progress and prospects of Strategy as Practice (SAP) research. Proposing four key directions for future research, the article lays out a vigorous agenda, driven by the constant innovation of strategy practice itself.

title: Adaptive spatio-temporal fusion network for high-frequency water quality forecasting
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Adaptive spatio-temporal fusion network for high-frequency water quality forecasting
detail.abstract: High-frequency water quality forecasting is essential for operational early warning and refined water-environment management. However, it remains challenging due to pronounced nonlinearity and non-stationarity, multi-scale temporal variability, cross-indicator heterogeneity, and event-driven disturbances. In this study, an adaptive spatio-temporal fusion network (STFusionNet) is proposed for high-frequency multi-indicator forecasting using 4-hourly automatic monitoring records from a dense lake-basin network (96 stations) spanning from June 17, 2021 to February 14, 2025. The forecasting task is structured as multi-horizon prediction with a 7-day historical input window (42 steps) and lead times of 12, 24, 48, 120, and 168 hours. STFusionNet combines a geographic k-nearest-neighbor graph (k = 6) with Gaussian distance weighting (σ = 20 km) and a learnable adaptive adjacency matrix to capture spatial dependencies. The model employs parallel temporal encoders to extract complementary representations, and adopts a gated fusion mechanism to dynamically aggregate multi-scale temporal features for joint forecasting of six key indicators. Comprehensive experiments benchmark STFusionNet against representative baselines (including CNN, TCN, LSTM, and iTransformer) using evaluation metrics such as Nash–Sutcliffe efficiency, root mean square error, and coefficient of determination. Results indicate that STFusionNet consistently achieves superior predictive performance across indicators and forecasting horizons, demonstrating robust improvements over both attention-based and conventional deep learning baselines. The proposed framework thus provides accurate and reliable support for real-time water quality monitoring and risk-informed management.

title: A High-Resolution Modeling Framework for Electric Vehicle Fleet Operation and Charging Planning with Photovoltaic Integration
affiliations: Rio de Janeiro State University, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN and Eletrobras

detail.title: A High-Resolution Modeling Framework for Electric Vehicle Fleet Operation and Charging Planning with Photovoltaic Integration
detail.abstract: This paper presents an innovative methodology for planning the operation of an electric vehicle (EV) fleet for public passenger transportation and its charging infrastructure with the integration of an on-grid photovoltaic (PV) system. Based on geographic coordinates, a model was developed to define the route profile, i.e., the vehicle speed cycle relative to travel time, applied to the case study. The selected case study and research correspond to the tourist route that connects the states of Rio de Janeiro and São Paulo, known as the Estrada Parque Paraty–Cunha, part of the historic Estrada Real, a well-known Brazilian route. The method is also applicable to the planning of future roads in terms of charging station allocation and accounts for traction forces and energy developed by the vehicle during displacement, including the effect of air density variation with altitude on aerodynamic drag. Through this methodology, it is possible to obtain instantaneous power and energy consumption throughout the route, thus enabling the planning of fleet operation and the corresponding energy supply system, with a focus on energy efficiency and environmental sustainability.

title: Intelligent Waste Monitoring in Industrial Environments Using Adaptive Computer Vision and Hybrid Edge–API Architecture
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Intelligent Waste Monitoring in Industrial Environments Using Adaptive Computer Vision and Hybrid Edge–API Architecture
detail.abstract: Industrial waste monitoring remains a challenging task due to adverse environmental conditions, heterogeneous materials, and the lack of reliable sensing solutions for continuous operation. This paper presents an intelligent computer vision system designed for real-time monitoring of industrial industrial waste containers operating in a mining environment. The proposed approach combines adaptive temporal analysis, domain-oriented heuristics, and a hybrid edge and API artificial intelligence architecture to detect disposal events, estimate bin occupancy, and classify disposed materials without relying on embedded physical sensors. Unlike conventional intelligent waste monitoring systems based on IoT sensors or purely data-driven deep learning models, the proposed system prioritizes operational robustness and deployment feasibility under uncontrolled industrial conditions. The architecture enables incremental volumetric estimation based on the visual evolution of occupancy, maintaining continuous operation through asynchronous semantic classification via external AI services. The system was deployed and validated at a real industrial facility of one of the world's largest mining companies operating in Brazil. Field results demonstrate stable performance under changing lighting conditions, occlusions, and environmental disturbances, enabling reliable monitoring in long-term operational scenarios. Overall, the results indicate that adaptive computer vision integrated with hybrid intelligent architectures represents a viable and scalable solution for intelligent waste management in industrial environments, contributing to the digital transformation of industrial monitoring processes.

title: A Novel Pyramid Framework for Analyzing the Sustainability of Urban Transportation
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN and Universiti Sains Malaysia (USM)

detail.title: A Novel Pyramid Framework for Analyzing the Sustainability of Urban Transportation
detail.abstract: In this study, a sustainable performance assessment that uses the pyramid framework is proposed, and a network directional distance function (NDDF) model is developed to evaluate sustainable performance and its subdimensions in bus transit systems. The subdimensions of sustainable performance encompass economic operation, the environment, equity, and safety. An empirical analysis was conducted using data from eight bus transit systems between 2014 and 2019. The findings reveal that, on average, the sustainable performance of all decision-making units (DMUs) is 0.90518. The performance in the subdimensions is 0.92213 for operation, 0.90262 for equity, 0.91076 for safety, and 0.96963 for environmental aspects. While bus transit systems demonstrate good performance in terms of the environment, they show lower performance in terms of equity and safety. To enhance the sustainable performance of bus transit systems, there is significant room for improvement amounting to approximately 9.738% in equity and 8.924% in safety. The results indicate that bus transit systems should prioritize safety and equity dimensions to reduce accidents and offer more services to non-full fare passengers. This study not only identifies bottlenecks, such as low safety performance, but also provides improvement strategies for different bus transit systems. The proposed model offers transit operators valuable insights into managerial performance, and it supports the advancement of sustainable transportation development.

title: The Entrepreneurial Team Formation Experience: Evidence from The PGA TOUR
affiliations: Southwestern Oklahoma State University, University of Central Oklahoma - Department of Economics and Southwestern Oklahoma State University

detail.title: The Entrepreneurial Team Formation Experience: Evidence from The PGA TOUR
detail.abstract: Detailed golf data from the PGA TOUR provides a unique opportunity to measure performance in the workplace, and in this case, how the choice to partner might inform what we know about entrepreneurial team formation. In 2017, the PGA TOUR created a new event in which two golfers compete as a team in two different formats, best ball and alternate shot. We use data on player ability and performance from the 2017 -19 PGA TOUR team event to determine how skill differences (or similarities) impact team performance. We also explore the weakest link effect and why an entrepreneur might partner with someone for personal reasons rather than an obvious complementary technical or professional proficiency. Our contributions have theoretical and practical implications for entrepreneurial team composition and formation strategies on performance.

title: Integrated service and partial-charging scheduling for electric ground-handling vehicles in airports: A two-stage adaptive large neighborhood search approach
affiliations: Tongji University, Tongji University, Tongji University, Tongji University, Tongji University and Tongji University

detail.title: Integrated service and partial-charging scheduling for electric ground-handling vehicles in airports: A two-stage adaptive large neighborhood search approach
detail.abstract: With increasing emphasis on sustainability and carbon reduction in the aviation industry, a growing number of airports have begun adopting electric ground-handling vehicles (EGHVs) to replace conventional fuel-powered ones, a transition that further increases the complexity of ground-handling vehicles (GHVs) scheduling due to their limited driving range and prolonged charging requirements. Existing studies on EGHVs scheduling rely on simplified charging assumptions, typically adopting a threshold-based full-charging strategy, in which vehicles are charged only when their battery levels fall below a predefined threshold and are charged to full capacity. Such simplifications limit operational flexibility and overlook the potential benefits of active partial-charging between consecutive service tasks. To address these issues, this paper considers the integrated scheduling of aircraft services and partial-charging of EGHVs under charging resource constraints, and develops a general mixed-integer program (MIP) model that provides a unified formulation of service assignment and charging decisions. Based on this model, a customized two-stage adaptive large neighborhood search (ALNS) algorithm is proposed, which decomposes the overall scheduling problem into a flight-vehicle assignment stage and a partial-charging decision stage, and efficiently explores the solution space through heuristic guidance and dynamic neighborhood search mechanisms. To evaluate its performance under various problem sizes and scheduling horizons, extensive computational experiments are conducted on large-scale instances randomly generated from the operational data of Shanghai Hongqiao International Airport. The results demonstrate that the proposed algorithm significantly outperforms the commercial solver Gurobi and several benchmark algorithms in terms of solution performance. Moreover, charging-strategy analysis confirms that the partial-charging strategy can achieve substantial cost savings compared with the threshold-based full-charging strategy.

title: A Collaborative Heuristic and Enhanced Black-winged Kite Algorithm for Solving 3D Bin Packing Problems in Complex Scenarios
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: A Collaborative Heuristic and Enhanced Black-winged Kite Algorithm for Solving 3D Bin Packing Problems in Complex Scenarios
detail.abstract: As solving 3D Bin Packing Problems (3D-BPP) involves the consideration of numerous types of items, different sizes and multiple constraints, the existing packing algorithms hardly meet demands for the balance among efficiency, accuracy and robustness in practical applications, such as warehouse management and intelligent manufacturing. In this study, a global-local collaborative optimization architecture that is inspired by the enhanced black-winged kite algorithm (BKA), has been proposed, called col-EBKA, to establish a stable and mappable continuous-discrete transformation mechanism that enables a deep coupling between global exploration of BKA and local optimization processes of heuristic strategies, thereby achieving a balance between search efficiency and accuracy and demonstrating great robustness in solving 3D-BPP. Moreover, a cooperative constraint combining a hyperplane constraint and a region-exclusive placement constraint (Hyperplane-Region Cooperative Constraint) has been defined to reserve exclusive space for special items such as fragile items, fresh food items, etc., thereby mitigating the risk of item damage. To verify the effectiveness of the proposed col-EBKA architecture in solving complex problems, experimental validations have been conducted on the Bischoff and Ratcliff benchmark dataset and a real-world packing case to demonstrate the performance superiority over exiting methods. Results have shown that col-EBKA has achieved an average space utilization rate of 92.69% on weakly heterogeneous datasets and 88.57% on strongly heterogeneous datasets, thereby exhibiting remarkable robustness. In the real-world packing case involving protected-item constraints, the proposed col-EBKA architecture has also excelled in good space utilization under HRCC, offering significant theoretical basis for e-commerce logistics and transportation using robots.

title: Three-Speed Banking Architecture Within Community Banks:,Stochastic Frontier Analysis of Cost Efficiency Divergence, 2015–2024

detail.title: Three-Speed Banking Architecture Within Community Banks:,Stochastic Frontier Analysis of Cost Efficiency Divergence, 2015–2024
detail.abstract: his paper extends the three-speed banking architecture framework to the interior of the community banking sector, testing whether technology-driven efficiency divergence previously documented between megabanks and mission-constrained institutions replicates within the $10 million–$10 billion asset tier. The analysis employs a stochastic frontier analysis (SFA) framework with a half-normal inefficiency distribution, estimated by maximum likelihood on an unbalanced panel of 50,804 FDIC institution-year observations spanning 2015–2024. Community banks are classified into three speed groups by asset scale: Speed 1 (small, <$100M, n=1,834 institutions), Speed 2 (core, $100M–$1B, n=4,504), and Speed 3 (upper, $1B–$10B, n=1,206). Three central findings emerge. First, the Cost Efficiency Ratio (CER) gap between Speed 1 and Speed 3 institutions widened from 10.6 percentage points in the pre-AI period (2015–2016) to 16.1 percentage points in the Generative AI era (Wave III, 2023–2024), a 52 percent relative increase. Second, SFA efficiency scores confirm directional divergence: Speed 1 mean efficiency declined from 0.941 in 2015 to 0.904 in 2024, while Speed 3 remained stable above 0.950. The estimated signal-to-noise ratio (λ = 0.713) confirms economically meaningful inefficiency variation across institutions. Third, unconditional quantile partial effects (RIF-OLS) following Firpo, Fortin, and Lemieux (2009) reveal that the Speed 1 efficiency penalty is distributional in character—rising monotonically from an insignificant -0.34 pp at the tenth percentile to +5.27 pp (p<0.001) at the ninetieth percentile—replicating the frontier-acceleration mechanism documented in prior megabank research rather than the floor-compression pattern observed among CDFI credit unions. These findings carry direct implications for financial stability policy: the three-speed architecture is endogenous to community banking and is not solely a product of the megabank versus community bank boundary.

title: Barriers to circular economy adoption in West Africa
affiliations: Excelia Business School, affiliation not provided to SSRN and University of Graz

detail.title: Barriers to circular economy adoption in West Africa
detail.abstract: This study examines barriers to circular economy adoption in West Africa (Côte d’Ivoire, Senegal, Guinea) through an institutional theory lens. An exploratory qualitative study of eight companies identifies barriers across eight categories, revealing that institutional voids—regulatory, normative, and market gaps—hinder circular economy adoption. Findings highlight weak coercive pressures, cultural resistance, and market immaturity, alongside the role of intrinsic leadership in overcoming systemic constraints. The paper contributes to institutional theory in emerging economies and offers recommendations for policymakers and businesses to strengthen regulations, awareness, and local infrastructure.

title: Statistical Hybrid Riemannian-Ensemble Dimensional Integration (SHREDI) Reveals Metabolic Arrest in Financial Manifolds
affiliations: North-West University

detail.title: Statistical Hybrid Riemannian-Ensemble Dimensional Integration (SHREDI) Reveals Metabolic Arrest in Financial Manifolds
detail.abstract: Financial stability frameworks assume that crises resemble ecological tipping points, where rising autocorrelation signals impending collapse. This paradigm fails for infrastructure-constrained markets, which exhibit a synchronisation paradox: behavioural convergence without volatility amplification. This study introduces the Statistical Hybrid Riemannian-Ensemble Dimensional Integration (SHREDI) framework to diagnose this condition, termed metabolic arrest. Integrating Random Forest classification with topological data analysis and Riemannian geometry, SHREDI analyses South African financial markets during sustained electricity load-shedding from January 2015 to December 2025 (N = 2,731 trading days). The study establishes that Stage 4 load-shedding, corresponding to a 4,000 MW generation deficit, constitutes a deterministic threshold: effective dimensionality collapses, autocorrelation declines rather than rises, and entropy bifurcates discontinuously at a magnitude consistent with the universal range documented across jamming transitions in physical systems. Machine learning achieves classification accuracy unprecedented in financial econometrics, and Fisher Information Gain confirms the transition from probabilistic regime overlap to deterministic constraint. These results invalidate ecological early-warning frameworks and establish that infrastructure-driven fragility belongs to the jammed universality class, requiring macroprudential surveillance to shift from monitoring weakening restoring forces to monitoring geometric constraints on market mobility.

title: Participation, Engagement, and Competency Development in Multicultural Virtual Management Education: Multi-Source Evidence from an 8-Week Program
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Participation, Engagement, and Competency Development in Multicultural Virtual Management Education: Multi-Source Evidence from an 8-Week Program
detail.abstract: This study examines the relationships among behavioral participation intensity, peer-assessed engagement quality, and team psychological safety and performance and developmental gains in a multicultural virtual management education program. Drawing on experiential learning theory and student engagement theory, we analyzed six data sources from an eight-week virtual International Business Strategy course involving undergraduate students from Mexico, Germany, and 11 other countries across eight cross-national teams (N = 69 participation records; N = 74 course grades; N = 46 matched pre-post pairs; N = 406 peer evaluations; N = 75 team leader evaluations; N = 80 reflection reports). We propose a participation–engagement–learning (PEL) framework that distinguishes participation intensity as a behavioral condition, engagement quality as a relational process, and competency development as a learning outcome. The results show that individual participation strongly predicts individual course grades but not independent team battle performance. Matched pre-post analyses indicated significant gains in cultural intelligence (d = 0.81, p < .001) and global leadership self-efficacy (d = 1.07, p < .001). Team psychological safety was positively associated with post-program cultural intelligence and leadership self-efficacy, whereas participation intensity was not. Reflection reports revealed identity disruption, collaborative meaning-making, and the reconstruction of leadership schemas.

title: An AI-Driven Learning Analytics Model for Evaluating Digital Competence of Vocational Teachers
affiliations: Shanxi Vocational University of Engineering Science and Technology, Shanxi Vocational University of Engineering Science and Technology, Shanxi Vocational University of Engineering Science and Technology and Shanxi Vocational University of Engineering Science and Technology

detail.title: An AI-Driven Learning Analytics Model for Evaluating Digital Competence of Vocational Teachers
detail.abstract: The rapid digital transformation of vocational education requires teachers to possess advanced digital competence to design, implement, and assess technology-enhanced learning. However, current evaluation approaches rely primarily on subjective surveys and manual observations, which limit accuracy, scalability, and real-time feedback. To address this gap, this study proposes an AI-driven learning analytics model for evaluating and predicting the digital competence of vocational teachers. The model integrates multimodal instructional data—including classroom interaction logs, technology-usage behaviors, resource-development traces, and performance indicators—based on the Digital Competence Framework for Vocational Teachers in China. A hybrid machine learning architecture combining feature engineering, attention-based representation learning, and gradient-boosted prediction is developed to classify competence levels across the framework’s eight dimensions. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed model significantly outperforms traditional assessment methods, achieving high accuracy and strong generalization in competence prediction. The study provides a scalable, data-driven solution for teacher development, offering practical implications for intelligent evaluation, personalized training, and digital-education reform.

title: Digital technologies for carbon emissions assessment in maritime ports: A bibliometric analysis
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Digital technologies for carbon emissions assessment in maritime ports: A bibliometric analysis
detail.abstract: The digitalization of maritime ports is transforming global logistics and trade by improving operational efficiency, safety, and sustainability. As ports face increasing pressure to handle growing cargo volumes, reduce environmental impacts, and remain competitive, integrating digital technologies such as the Internet of Things, artificial intelligence and digital twins has become critical. These technologies enable real-time data sharing, predictive maintenance and automated procedures and cargo handling, leading to faster turnaround times and better decisions. Digital platforms also facilitate collaboration among port stakeholders, including terminal operators, shipowners, logistics companies, and regulators. Despite progress in port operations, using these technologies to assess carbon emissions remains at an early stage, while challenges such as cybersecurity risks, high implementation costs, and the need for standardized protocols persist. This paper reviews the current state of port digitalization for emissions monitoring, evaluates its benefits and challenges, and outlines strategies to support resilient, smart, and low-carbon maritime hubs.

title: Research on Adoption Strategies of Social E-commerce Recommendation Systems in Dual-Channel Supply Chains
affiliations: Zhongyuan University of Technology, Zhongyuan University of Technology and Zhongyuan University of Technology

detail.title: Research on Adoption Strategies of Social E-commerce Recommendation Systems in Dual-Channel Supply Chains
detail.abstract: In the context of the rapid rise of social e-commerce, this paper constructs a game-theoretic model for a dual-channel supply chain consisting of a manufacturer and an online retailer. It investigates the manufacturer's strategy for adopting a third-party recommendation system in its direct sales channel. The model innovatively introduces two core variables—social interaction effect intensity and social channel commission rate—to systematically analyze the manufacturer's adoption decisions and the game equilibrium among supply chain members under different payment schemes (Cost-Per-Sale CPS and Cost-Per-Click CPC). By solving a three-stage Stackelberg game across seven scenarios, this study finds that when the retailer has already adopted a recommendation system, the manufacturer's dominant strategy is to forgo adoption and "free-ride." When the retailer does not adopt, the manufacturer's decision depends on the recommendation strength and cost. The social interaction effect amplifies the impact of recommendation strength, thereby increasing the manufacturer's willingness to adopt, while the social channel commission rate increases the cost burden, suppressing adoption willingness. Furthermore, the manufacturer's preference between CPS and CPC shifts dynamically with the adoption context and recommendation cost. The study also clarifies the decision boundaries for achieving a win-win outcome for both the manufacturer and retailer. The conclusions provide a theoretical basis and managerial insights for enterprises formulating recommendation system adoption strategies and channel coordination mechanisms in the social e-commerce environment.

title: Blockchain-Powered QoS Management in HEVC Video Streaming
affiliations: Sultan Moulay Slimane University and Sultan Moulay Slimane University

detail.title: Blockchain-Powered QoS Management in HEVC Video Streaming
detail.abstract: As the demand for high-resolution video streaming continues to grow, maintaining stable Quality of Service has become increasingly challenging, particularly under dynamic and congested network conditions. This paper proposes a blockchain-enabled framework to enhance QoS for High Efficiency Video Coding (HEVC) video transmission by integrating smart contracts and a token-based allocation scheme to dynamically negotiate bandwidth, prioritize critical video packets, and allocate resources fairly and transparently. The decentralized architecture improves key QoS metrics, including latency, jitter, packet delivery ratio, throughput, and fairness index, as well as video quality metrics such as PSNR, SSIM, and VMAF, without relying on centralized control. By enabling real-time and verifiable decision-making based on network conditions and user priorities, the proposed system reduces latency, jitter, and packet loss while maintaining stable video quality. Extensive experiments were conducted to evaluate network-level QoS and perceptual video quality, and the results indicate notable improvements over baseline HEVC streaming, including up to 40% reduction in latency, 50% reduction in jitter, gains of approximately 2.1 dB in PSNR, 0.04 in SSIM, and 8–10 points in VMAF. Additional comparisons with edge-assisted QoS approaches and token-based streaming platforms such as Theta demonstrate improved fairness and perceptual quality under congested conditions. These findings suggest that blockchain-enabled QoS management can provide reliable and adaptive video streaming performance and is suitable for real-time applications such as telemedicine, online learning, and live broadcasting.

title: Precision Inversion under Majority Attacks: A Unix-Inspired Trust-Adaptive Digital Twin Framework for Large-Scale IoT
affiliations: DKTE Society's Textile & Engineering Institute and SRM Institute of Science and Technology

detail.title: Precision Inversion under Majority Attacks: A Unix-Inspired Trust-Adaptive Digital Twin Framework for Large-Scale IoT
detail.abstract: Large-scale Internet of Things (IoT) deployments increasingly operate in hostile environments where malicious traffic represents the majority of network activity. In these "majority-attack" regimes, traditional unsupervised Intrusion Detection Systems (IDS) suffer from precision collapse and model drift due to the failure of the rarity assumption. This work presents the system-level implementation and empirical validation of a Unix-inspired, trust-adaptive Digital Twin security framework designed specifically for high-contamination IoT environments.The framework operationalizes a "Digital Twin" architecture where heterogeneous devices are abstracted as digital nodes under the principle that "Everything is a File." These nodes are organized into hierarchical families to govern parent-child and sibling relationships. To prevent identity-mimicking and spoofing, the system utilizes BLAKE3-based fingerprinting and HKDF-based key derivation to generate unique, tamper-evident composite identities. Security is enforced through a Trust-Adaptive Dynamic Key Management (T-DKM) layer and an AI-assisted veto mechanism using Isolation Forest, which modulates detection thresholds through asymmetric trust evolution.Evaluations on the BoT-IoT, UNSW-NB15, and ToN_IoT datasets—supplemented by behavior-driven spectral clustering—validate the framework’s ability to achieve "precision inversion" and linear scalability under adversarial dominance. While public benchmarks provide a conservative baseline, synthetic stress tests demonstrate that the framework’s full potential for strict Zero Trust architecture is realized through deterministic identity grouping.

title: A Comprehensive Review of Feature Selection Strategies for Machine Learning Based Android Malware Detection
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: A Comprehensive Review of Feature Selection Strategies for Machine Learning Based Android Malware Detection
detail.abstract: The emergence of even more advanced attacks of mobile malware that have been trying to steal user credentials and other important data has also been accompanied by the concept of mobile smartphone use that is projected to be in the billions across the globe. With high dimensionality of features in modern malware datasets, effective feature selection is important to perfor-mance as well as efficiency of machine learning (ML) models, which often involve selecting most relevant features from a potentially large set of features.

title: 1 iOS Lifestyle Medicine FHIR Implementation Guide: A Multi-Vendor Data Interoperability Framework with Documented Terminology Gaps
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: 1 iOS Lifestyle Medicine FHIR Implementation Guide: A Multi-Vendor Data Interoperability Framework with Documented Terminology Gaps
detail.abstract: Background: Consumer wearable devices collect clinical-grade physiological data directly by patients, yet less than 5% of this patient-generated health data (PGHD) reaches clinical systems.  The European Health Data Space (EHDS) Regulation 2025/327 mandates standardized health​ data exchange, creating urgent need for validated transformation frameworks. Objective: To develop and validate a FHIR R4 Implementation Guide enabling multi-vendor wearable data transformation for lifestyle medicine, documenting terminology gaps across seven vendor ecosystems. Methods: We developed FHIR profiles, extensions, and ConceptMaps using a multi-layer architecture covering eleven domains (six lifestyle medicine pillars and five wearable-specific). Technical validation included HL7 IG Publisher compilation, FHIR Validator conformance testing, and systematic terminology verification. Results: The IG comprises 74 profiles, 50 extensions, 14 CodeSystems, 174 ValueSets, and 28 ConceptMaps (546 artifacts). A two-phase terminology audit refined 1,173 custom codes to 718 without standard direct equivalents, including genuine gaps (RMSSD, pNN50), wearable-specific metrics, and granularity not yet addressed by LOINC or SNOMED CT. Build validation produces 23 errors (all IPS upstream) and 73 warnings (97% non-actionable). Of six core HRV metrics, only SDNN has a LOINC code (80404-7). The multi-layer architecture achieved 75% weighted reuse across seven vendor ecosystems. Conclusions: This work extends the HL7 Physical Activity IG’s “Temporary Codes” pattern into a semantic convergence buffer—a vendor-neutral intermediary CodeSystem with outbound ConceptMap coverage to LOINC, SNOMED CT, and OMOP enabling multi-vendor semantic convergence. The 75% weighted reuse and iterative terminology audits progressively reduce custom codes as standards mature. All profiles are vendor-agnostic and EHDS-compliant.

title: Identifying Inflation Trend, Cycle, and Persistence in Korea from the Term Structure of Inflation Expectations
affiliations: Bank of Korea and Korea University

detail.title: Identifying Inflation Trend, Cycle, and Persistence in Korea from the Term Structure of Inflation Expectations
detail.abstract: This paper develops a framework for identifying inflation dynamics using theterm structure of inflation expectations. We integrate anunobserved-components (UC) model of inflation with a dynamic Nelson--Siegel(DNS) representation of the inflation expectation curve (IEC). In theresulting UC--DNS model, the level, slope, and curvature of the IEC correspondto trend inflation, cyclical inflation, and persistence.Estimation using Korean survey expectations and inflation shows that the UC--DNS model ispreferred over the conventional UC model and produces substantially differentestimates of trend inflation, indicating that information embedded in the IEChelps identify the inflation trend. The results further show that IEC-impliedcyclical inflation is actively revised in response to previously unperceivedcyclical shocks. Long-run expectations closely track trend inflation, whilecyclical inflation is negatively correlated with its persistence, implyingfaster mean reversion when inflation rises above trend.

title: Performance of Gridded Rainfall Products in Reproducing Gauge-Observation rainfall for Agricultural Management in Africa
affiliations: Norwegian University of Life Sciences, Norwegian University of Life Sciences, affiliation not provided to SSRN, University of Zambia (UNZA), Gulu University and Norwegian University of Life Sciences

detail.title: Performance of Gridded Rainfall Products in Reproducing Gauge-Observation rainfall for Agricultural Management in Africa
detail.abstract: Agricultural systems need transformation to cope with multiple challenges including climate change and variability. Deriving understanding of climatic conditions to guide the transformation is constrained by data unavailability and quality problems attributed to sparsity of meteorological stations. This study analyzed reliability of selected gridded-rainfall products: Global Precipitation Climate Centre (GPCC), Climate Hazards Infra-Red Precipitation with Stations (CHIRPS) and Climate Resource Unit (CRU) to reproduce station-observed rainfall. Moreover, assessing the data skills in capturing rainfall characteristics and identify zones of climate-related stressors/risks influencing agricultural and water resources management across spatial continuum in Zambia and Uganda. Graphical and statistical techniques were used to evaluate the reliability, whereas statistical and geospatial techniques to assess skills of gridded-data to delineate potential zones of climate features such as climate-related constraints to rain-fed Agricultural production. The results revealed gridded data adequately reproduced rain-gauge rainfalls with strong and significant correlation at monthly scale in Zambia (r ≥ 0, 92, p < 0, 05) and Uganda (0.80 ≤ r ≤ 0.85, p < 0.05). In addition, the data captured spatial patterns of the main rainfall characteristics and zones of rainfall-seasonality. Zones of trends in seasonal and annual rainfalls were delineated to guide prescribing or piloting Climate-smart agriculture technologies. Across the two countries, GPCC data performed best followed by CHIRPS and CRU.TS. We conclude that though with minor discrepancies, the gridded rainfall products are promising for selection as surrogate or to complement gauging-stations’ rainfall in areas with limited or lack meteorological stations.

title: Money as a Constraint: Settlement Reliability, Safe Assets, and Nominal Contracting

detail.title: Money as a Constraint: Settlement Reliability, Safe Assets, and Nominal Contracting
detail.abstract: Macroeconomic models typically assume that once prices are observed, nominal contracts translate mechanically into real settlement. This paper studies the institutional margin embedded in that assumption. I introduce a state-dependent settlement parameter governing whether nominal promises translate into real allocations as intended. Variation in this parameter produces what I call constraint volatility. The framework generates a new asset-pricing implication: nominal assets with more reliable settlement command equilibrium price premia. This provides a reinterpretation of safe-asset demand and convenience yields in modern financial markets. The analysis extends the microfoundations of money literature by examining the stability of the institutional environment that nominal contracting presumes.

title: Productivity Dynamics of Japan’s Regional Banks After the First-Interest Rate Hike: A Two-Stage Network DEA and Malmquist Analysis
affiliations: Soka University

detail.title: Productivity Dynamics of Japan’s Regional Banks After the First-Interest Rate Hike: A Two-Stage Network DEA and Malmquist Analysis
detail.abstract: This paper examines the structural transformation of Japan’s regional banking sector following the historical termination of the negative interest rate policy (NIRP) in March 2024. Using this policy pivot as a natural experiment, we investigate the immediate re-optimization of bank intermediation models through a two-stage network Data Envelopment Analysis (DEA) and Malmquist productivity indices. We decompose the production process into two analytically distinct dimensions: lending intermediation (deposit-to-loan transformation) and earnings intermediation (loan-to-net-interest-income conversion).,Utilizing bank-level data for Regional Banks I and II from FY2023–FY2024, our results reveal a profound stage asymmetry in post-hike productivity dynamics. While the earnings stage exhibited broad-based productivity gains—driven by a significant outward shift in the net-interest-income (NII) generation frontier—lending-stage productivity remained stagnant or deteriorated across all regions. Critically, these dynamics are moderated by regional market concentration, as measured by the Herfindahl–Hirschman Index (HHI): banks in highly competitive environments faced substantial frictions in loan repricing, leading to attenuated productivity gains compared to those in concentrated markets.,These findings suggest that monetary normalization permeates the banking sector primarily through an asset-repricing windfall rather than a fundamental reactivation of deposit-funded credit supply. The study underscores a selective and asymmetric transmission of monetary policy and provides critical implications for financial supervisors regarding the strategic viability and monitoring of regional banking models in a positive-interest-rate environment.

title: The Emission Paradox of Autonomous Vehicles: A Free-Riding Mechanism in Mixed Traffic
affiliations: Shanghai University

detail.title: The Emission Paradox of Autonomous Vehicles: A Free-Riding Mechanism in Mixed Traffic
detail.abstract: It is widely assumed that introducing eco-driving autonomous vehicles (AVs) will monotonically reduce traffic carbon emissions. This letter reveals a counter-intuitive emission paradox in mixed traffic flow. By modeling the heterogeneous utility functions of AVs (emission internalizers) and human-driven vehicles (HVs, time optimizers), we identify a distinct "free-riding" mechanism: HVs systematically exploit the eco-friendly, larger safety gaps maintained by AVs through aggressive cut-in behaviors. Analytical derivations demonstrate that at low AV penetration rates, the negative externality generated by these HV-induced perturbations far outweighs the direct emission benefits of AVs. We validate this theoretical finding using an extended METANET model calibrated to a real-world freeway section in Shanghai. The results exhibit a pronounced inverted-U relationship between AV penetration and total carbon emissions, suggesting that early-stage AV deployment may inadvertently exacerbate environmental costs without proper policy interventions.

title: Sustained House Price Booms and Banking Crisis Risk:,Causal Evidence from a Global Panel
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Sustained House Price Booms and Banking Crisis Risk:,Causal Evidence from a Global Panel

keywords.keywords: Banking crises · House price booms · HP filter · Double Machine Learning · Early-warning systems

detail.abstract: Not all housing booms carry the same banking crisis risk. Using a global panel of 131 countries and an empirical pipeline combining Double Machine Learning, doubly robust AIPW, Causal Forest, and staggered difference-in-differences, this paper provides evidence that HP-filter booms — which capture persistent deviations from long-run trend — raise next-year banking crisis probability by approximately 3.8 percentage points, while Hamilton-filter booms — which capture short-run price acceleration — are statistically null within the same common estimation sample and with the same covariate set. This is the paper’s central finding: the choice of boom definition, a consequential empirical design decision that the literature has treated as secondary, substantially conditions whether an early-warning signal is detected. The HP effect is stable across a comprehensive robustness grid, including an expanding-window treatment definition that constructs boom thresholds from information available only at the time of classification, directly addressing the look-ahead concern raised against standard HP-based indicators. The signal materialises within one year of boom onset, remains significant at the two-year horizon, and closes by year three. As a secondary and hypothesis-generating finding, Causal Forest variable importance analysis ranks the current account balance first among cross-country moderators, though the Best Linear Projection does not resolve a statistically significant linear gradient and the mechanism remains an open empirical question. These results suggest that crisis-prediction frameworks calibrated to short-run momentum may underweight the persistent imbalance component of housing booms that carries the robust signal.

title: Socio-environmental conflicts, Food Sovereignty and Food Security in Antioquia, Colombia: a stakeholder perspective
affiliations: Universidad de Antioquia, Universidad de Antioquia, Universidad de Antioquia, affiliation not provided to SSRN, Universidad de Antioquia and Universidad de Antioquia

detail.title: Socio-environmental conflicts, Food Sovereignty and Food Security in Antioquia, Colombia: a stakeholder perspective
detail.abstract: This article examines socio-environmental conflicts in Antioquia based on the Food and Nutrition Profile conducted in 2019, focusing on their impact on food security and food sovereignty. The study employs a qualitative approach grounded in the methodology proposed by Strauss and Corbin and the constructivist perspective of Charmaz, for which 193 interviews were conducted across nine subregions of the department. The results identify five socio-environmental conflicts, classified into the following categories: mining and armed conflict, land tenure, deforestation, urbanization and industrialization, and tourism. Mining, both legal and illegal, has generated severe environmental impacts such as water source contamination and deforestation, and it creates social tensions, particularly due to the involvement of illegal armed groups. Conflicts over land tenure— driven by the expansion of monocultures and extensive cattle ranching—have degraded soils and reduced agricultural production. Deforestation, primarily caused by mining and livestock activities, also contributes to biodiversity loss and soil erosion. Additionally, urbanization has displaced traditional agriculture, increased pressure on natural resources, and exacerbated pollution, affecting public health. Finally, tourism generates territorial conflicts related to inadequate waste management and food price speculation, affecting both the environment and the local economy. The study concludes that these conflicts, stemming from the control of natural resources, have profound implications for food security in the subregions of Antioquia, and their resolution requires an interdisciplinary approach involving communities, academia, and government.
